primary_claim: Gradient routing (masking gradients to localize computation, e.g. via the Expand-Route-Ablate scheme) enables more robust removal of capabilities under partial/imperfect data labels than data filtering, RMU, or DEMix baselines, and provides scalable oversight by localizing then activating desired sub-policies.

effect.metric: CE loss increase (nats) after retraining on forget data
effect.value: 0.18-nat increase in virology CE loss vs 0.03-nat increase in non-virology CE loss

contradicts_or_qualifies: Conventional unlearning methods suppress behavior rather than truly remove underlying capabilities/circuitry, per Deeb & Roger (2024), Sheshadri et al. (2024), and Łucki et al. (2024)
stated_future_work: Developing RL applications of gradient routing further
What kinds of environments admit this kind of scalable-oversight-via-localization solution
What it would look like to scale this solution to real-world alignment challenges
limitations_stated: No established best practices for applying gradient routing; extensive hyperparameter tuning needed (which tokens to route, how much of the network, learning rates, regularization)
Meaningful hit to retain-set performance (alignment tax) remains even after tuning
Entangled capabilities resist separate localization, increasing the alignment tax
Tuning cost may be prohibitive for larger models
quote: When labels are limited, we observe that Expand, Route, Ablate outperforms other methods, including data filtering.
